pr.body: Interpolating queries as the initial step. Fixes #107530
pr.title: Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process

raw_findings.body: Each split request receives ad hoc filters more than once, unnecessarily inflating and altering the LogQL selector. Sharded requests also pass through this extra interpolation when they delegate to runSplitQuery.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Split-query execution sends repeatedly interpolated target expressions instead of the original single-interpolation query.
raw_findings.impact: Each split request receives ad hoc filters more than once, unnecessarily inflating and altering the LogQL selector. Sharded requests also pass through this extra interpolation when they delegate to runSplitQuery.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch eagerly calls applyTemplateVariables while constructing split targets without preventing the normal DataSourceWithBackend execution path from applying the same transformation again.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Separate preprocessing needed for splitting from backend interpolation, or mark the generated subrequest as already interpolated and skip applyTemplateVariables during its execution so each target is processed exactly once.
raw_findings.title: Avoid applying template variables again in the backend execution path
raw_findings.trigger: Enable Loki query splitting and run a query with one or more ad hoc filters; the preprocessed target is subsequently passed to LokiDatasource.runQuery, whose inherited backend query path applies template variables again.

raw_findings.body: The test passes while production can apply template variables twice and duplicate ad hoc filters on every split request, leaving the introduced execution-path regression undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unit-test assertions cover only the preprocessed in-memory request and cannot detect defects introduced by the actual backend-query pipeline.
raw_findings.impact: The test passes while production can apply template variables twice and duplicate ad hoc filters on every split request, leaving the introduced execution-path regression undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The regression test stubs the method that contains the production execution boundary instead of observing the request after that boundary.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a real runQuery/backend request spy or mock the backend transport below super.query, include scoped variables and ad hoc filters, and assert the final outgoing target plus the number of interpolation/filter applications.
raw_findings.title: Add a regression test that exercises backend interpolation for split queries
raw_findings.trigger: Run the newly added interpolation test as written; replacing datasource.runQuery prevents LokiDatasource.runQuery and its inherited backend interpolation from executing, and the test does not include ad hoc filters.

finding.title: Avoid applying template variables again in the backend execution path
finding.trigger: Enable Loki query splitting and run a query with one or more ad hoc filters; the preprocessed target is subsequently passed to LokiDatasource.runQuery, whose inherited backend query path applies template variables again.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that applyTemplateVariables is applied twice is incorrect. Looking at the code flow: runSplitQuery calls applyTemplateVariables at line 299, then passes the interpolated queries to runSplitGroupedQueries which calls datasource.runQuery (line 180). runQuery is defined at line 350-357 and simply calls super.query() with transformBackendResult - it does NOT call applyTemplateVariables again. The DataSourceWithBackend.query() method does call applyTemplateVariables, but runSplitQuery bypasses the normal query() path by calling runQuery() directly. The shardQuerySplitting path also applies variables once in runShardSplitQuery (line 52) before calling runSplitQuery, but runSplitQuery receives already-interpolated queries and the test at line 112 confirms applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times total (once per query variant), not doubled.

finding.title: Add a regression test that exercises backend interpolation for split queries
finding.trigger: Run the newly added interpolation test as written; replacing datasource.runQuery prevents LokiDatasource.runQuery and its inherited backend interpolation from executing, and the test does not include ad hoc filters.
finding.verifier_reason: The test correctly validates the interpolation behavior. The mock of runQuery at line 83 is intentional - the test verifies that queries are interpolated BEFORE being passed to runQuery by checking the targets in the mock calls (lines 85-86). The test confirms the expr and step are properly interpolated. The claim that this misses 'backend interpolation' is unfounded because runQuery() does not perform additional interpolation - it just calls super.query() with transformation. The test adequately covers the new interpolation logic introduced by the patch.
